docRequirement: `commands.md:13` binds the whole command-invocation parse: "A command is only recognized at the start of your message. Text that follows the command name becomes its arguments. As of v2.1.199, [skills](/docs/en/skills#pass-arguments-to-skills) are the exception: a skill invocation followed by more skills, such as `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ`, loads every skill named at the start and passes the trailing text to each as arguments. Up to six skills can be chained." `skills.md:462`/`:464` sharpen it: "Claude Code expands the first skill plus up to five more stacked after it. Expansion stops at the first token that isn't an inline user-invocable skill ... That token and everything after it become the argument text for every expanded skill." So: a leading RUN of skill commands (max 6), one shared `$ARGUMENTS` string given to EVERY expanded skill, and the run terminated by the first non-(inline user-invocable skill) token. Non-skill commands keep the one-command rule.
current: One leading command is matched and everything after it is argument text, for every command type including skills. `apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/custom-slash-command-submission.ts:25-27` is a single `commands.find(...)` on the trimmed input; `:30-33` returns `{ message: invocation.slice(command.label.length).trim(), customSlashCommandId: command.id }`, and the return type at `:7-10` is singular by construction (`customSlashCommandId: CustomSlashCommandId`). The sibling menu entry point `customSlashCommandMenuSubmission` (`:12-18`) is singular too, so there is no second composer surface. The wire is singular from there down: `FreeFormInput.tsx:162` prop, `:1425` call, `ChatDisplay.tsx:284`/`:1501`/`:1513`, `AppShellContext.tsx:102`, `App.tsx:1225`/`:1336`, `ChatPage.tsx:805`/`:807`, `apps/electron/src/shared/types.ts:385`, and finally `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:310` `SEND_MESSAGE(..., customSlashCommandId?: CustomSlashCommandId)` — one optional scalar, not an array. The handler body at `:317-343` resolves exactly that one id via `sessionManager.resolveCustomSlashCommand` (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16080`, one `commandId`), then sets `message = args ? `${command.label} ${args}` : command.label` and `modelMessage = command.body.replace(/\$ARGUMENTS|\{\{args\}\}/g, () => args)` (`:334-335`). A skill command's body is `[skill:<reference>] $ARGUMENTS` (`packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:302-304`), so typing `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ` produces the model message `[skill:skill-a] /skill-b do XYZ`. The agent then parses one skill: `parseSkillMentionOccurrences` (`packages/shared/src/mentions/index.ts:52-54`) finds only the `[skill:skill-a]` marker, and `BaseAgent.extractSkillInvocations` (`packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2289-2339`) materializes that one; `/skill-b` survives as literal prose in the argument text. Nothing anywhere implements a run, a cap or a stop rule: `grep -ranE 'chained|chaining|stacked skills|multiple commands'` over `packages` and `apps` hits only shell-command chaining, plugin-dependency chains and promise chains. The stop rule's own inputs do exist — `selectSkillSlashCommands` (`custom-commands.ts:436-456`) already drops `userInvocable === false` at `:443`, so composer-list membership is exactly "inline user-invocable skill", and there is no forked-subagent skill mode at all (`grep -ran 'forkedSubagent|subagentSkill|run-in-subagent'` over `packages/shared/src` and `apps/electron/src`: zero hits).
divergence:
Three deltas, all on the leading-run parse; none on argument expansion, which is already correct for a single skill.

1. RUN LENGTH. We match one command; the doc requires a run of up to six when the first is a skill. This is not a wrong key name or a wrong value — the loop does not exist, and the singular `customSlashCommandId` type makes it unrepresentable end to end.

2. ARGUMENT DISTRIBUTION. The doc gives the SAME trailing text to every expanded skill. Our nearest native equivalent, `[skill:...]` mentions, PARTITIONS text between markers instead: `runtimeSkillArguments` (`packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:606-617`) is "Arguments following the last matching `[skill:...]` reference, up to the next skill mention", so on `[skill:a] [skill:b] do XYZ` skill-a gets `""` and skill-b gets `do XYZ`. That partition semantics is CORRECT for the model-emitted path (`extractModelSkillInvocations`, `base-agent.ts:2166-2188`, where the model writes a distinct task per marker) and must not be changed. The stacked-command fix therefore has to emit the shared text after EACH marker — `[skill:a] do XYZ\n[skill:b] do XYZ` — which the existing partition logic then reads back as `do XYZ` for both. No edit to `runtime-skill-content.ts` is needed, and that is the load-bearing detail: the naive composition `[skill:a] [skill:b] do XYZ` would silently give the first skill empty arguments.

3. CAP AND STOP RULE. Neither exists, because there is no run to bound. The stop condition reduces cleanly to `custom:skill:`-prefixed membership of the composer's own command list (non-user-invocable skills never enter it, `custom-commands.ts:443`); the doc's forked-subagent clause has no analogue today and would only become live if a subagent skill mode is ever added.

change.what: Make the submission plural: replace `customSlashCommandId: CustomSlashCommandId` (:9) with `customSlashCommandIds: readonly CustomSlashCommandId[]`, length 1 for every non-stacked case. In `customSlashCommandInputSubmission` (:20-34) keep the existing single `commands.find` for the FIRST match; then, only when that match's id is a skill command id, loop: repeatedly re-run the same label match against the remaining tail, appending ids while (a) the next token matches a command in `commands`, (b) that command's id is skill-prefixed, and (c) fewer than MAX_STACKED_SKILL_COMMANDS ids have been collected. Stop at the first token that fails any of those; `message` is that token and everything after it, trimmed — shared, not partitioned. De-duplicate ids (the same skill twice must not double-materialize). `customSlashCommandMenuSubmission` (:12-18) returns a one-element array unchanged.

Add `export const MAX_STACKED_SKILL_COMMANDS = 6` (docs: first plus five more) and `export function isSkillSlashCommandId(id: string): boolean` returning `id.startsWith(`${CUSTOM_SLASH_COMMAND_PREFIX}skill:`)`. There is no such predicate today — the prefix is only ever minted, never tested — and the renderer and the server both need the same one so the stack rule cannot drift between them. Carry the `commands.md:13` / `skills.md:464` quotes in the doc comment, per this repo's citation rule.

Widen the 7th positional parameter to `customSlashCommandIds?: CustomSlashCommandId | readonly CustomSlashCommandId[]` and normalize to an array on entry, so an older/remote client sending the scalar still works. Then: reject (throw `custom-slash-command-stack-invalid`) when the array has more than MAX_STACKED_SKILL_COMMANDS entries, or has more than one entry and any entry is not `isSkillSlashCommandId` — the doc's exception is skills only. Resolve each id in order through the existing `sessionManager.resolveCustomSlashCommand(key, id, args)` (unchanged signature; MCP-prompt and workflow branches stay single-id by the guard above). Compose `message = [...labels].join(' ') + (args ? ` ${args}` : '')` so the transcript shows `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ`, and `modelMessage = bodies.map(body => body.replace(/\$ARGUMENTS|\{\{args\}\}/g, () => args)).join('\n')` — the SAME `args` into every body, which yields `[skill:a] do XYZ\n[skill:b] do XYZ` and is what makes `runtimeSkillArguments` hand both skills the identical text. Keep `command.model` handling on the first resolved command only (a stack of skills has at most one model hint in practice; last-wins would silently reorder model switches).
Change the trailing parameter to `customSlashCommandIds?: readonly CustomSlashCommandId[]`. Preload/IPC pass-through only — no logic.

Rename the 4th `onSubmit` argument to the array and forward `submission.customSlashCommandIds` at both call sites. No ordering change: the custom-command branch must stay where it is, after the `!` shell branch and before `parseMentions`.

blastRadius: CROSSES THE RENDERER/SERVER WIRE BOUNDARY — a risk trigger in this repo. `RPC_CHANNELS.sessions.SEND_MESSAGE` is a positional-argument channel and its 7th parameter changes shape (`packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:310`; client side `apps/electron/src/shared/types.ts:385`). Accepting `scalar | array` is what keeps an older client or the headless `nessy-server` path working; without that widening this is a breaking wire change. It is a WIRE change only, not a persistence change: no id array is written to a session file — the handler collapses everything into `message` and `modelMessage` before persistence, so no migration and no schema version bump. Also frozen: `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/adjacent-backend-frozen-contract.test.ts:653-681` plus its fixture `fixtures/adjacent-backends/rpc-and-backends.json:252` assert the exact positional call and a single resolved key; both must be extended, not replaced. Unchanged by design: `SessionManager.resolveCustomSlashCommand` (`SessionManager.ts:16080`) and its interface row (`packages/server-core/src/handlers/session-manager-interface.ts:144`) stay single-id — the loop lives in the RPC handler, so `packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/custom-slash-command-boundary.test.ts` (11 call sites) needs no edit. `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.custom-slash-command.test.ts` stubs the resolver and will see N calls instead of 1. Downstream of the composed model message, the agent path already handles N skills and needs no change: `parseSkillMentionOccurrences` (`mentions/index.ts:52`), `BaseAgent.extractSkillInvocations` (`base-agent.ts:2289-2339`), `latestSkillSelections`, `runtimeSkillArguments` (`runtime-skill-content.ts:607`) and `assertSkillInvocationBudget` (`runtime-skill-content.ts:272`, a byte cap on the persisted invocation snapshot — six materialized skills at up to 256 KB of body each can trip it, so the cap of six is also what keeps this inside budget). Imported-plugin paths are touched indirectly: plugin-provided skills mint the same `custom:skill:<name>` ids via `selectSkillSlashCommands`, so a stack may mix native, bundled and plugin skills; `custom:plugin:*`, `custom:plugin-workflow:*`, `custom:workflow:*` and `custom:mcp:*` ids must be excluded from stacking by the guard, since `resolveCustomSlashCommand`'s MCP branch consumes `args` itself (`:16096-16111`) and the workflow branch dispatches `args` as `{input}` (`:16146-16159`) — neither can share a tail with a sibling.
userImpact: Observable today, in the Electron composer, on the exact input the doc names. A user who types `/write-tests /fix-issue 123` and presses Enter gets ONE skill loaded (`write-tests`) with the literal string `/fix-issue 123` as its arguments; the second skill's instructions never enter the turn. It fails silently and plausibly: the transcript shows `/write-tests /fix-issue 123`, the `/` menu lists both skills, and the model receives `/fix-issue` as prose, so it may or may not choose to emit `[skill:fix-issue]` itself on a later turn — meaning the user sometimes gets the second skill a turn late and sometimes not at all, with no error either way. Anyone following Claude's own skills documentation, or a plugin README that assumes stacking, hits this. Secondary surface: the argument text is also wrong for the one skill that does load — it receives `/fix-issue 123` instead of `123`, so a skill whose body uses `$1` or a declared argument name gets `/fix-issue` as its first positional value.
